Trial record · 2026-09-22 · feat/leaders-theme · PR #53

Ranza, in the Leaders direction

The workspace and both sign-in screens now carry the Leaders portal's design language: deep emerald on an ivory canvas, floating glass panels, large light titles, soft card rows and generous radii. The domain, routes and permissions are untouched.

Verdict: the shared kit in packages/ui carries the look, so every screen changed at once rather than page by page. Seven small, deliberate departures from Leaders are listed below with their reasons, along with ten defects found and fixed on the screens that were restyled.

pnpm checkGreen
Unit tests99 passing
Browser suite9 of 9 pass, not in one run
Languages checkedEN · TR · AR

The reference

Leaders for the workspace, EduBoard for sign-in

Leaders: floating glass rail and bar, a breadcrumb over a large light title, count cards with big soft numerals, rows as rounded cards. EduBoard: a framed sign-in sheet with an inset showcase panel.

Where it departs from Leaders

Seven departures, each with a reason

Leaders hasHereWhy
The security line under the formRemoved“Protected by enterprise-grade row-level security…” changes no decision a person makes at that moment. The standing rule is that security claims appear only where they change an action.
The padlock in the cornerRemovedOrnament that asserts security without saying anything. Deleting it loses nothing.
Leaders' sign-in compositionEduBoard's insteadAsked for after the first pass: the framed sheet and inset showcase panel of EduBoard's sign-in, in Ranza's emerald and gold. The gold swoosh became thin gold lines so the slogan stays legible, and the ambient radial glow is gone.
Bronze sub-slogan #a48166Darkened to #8a684dThe reference colour is 3.4:1 on the ivory canvas; body text needs 4.5:1. Same hue, 4.83:1.
Letter-spaced headings and capsLatin onlyAny letter-spacing makes the browser drop Arabic's joined letterforms. One rule in the theme sets Arabic to zero over every tracking utility, instead of an rtl: exception on each.
preferred_locale cookieNot carried overLeaders' middleware reads it. Ranza has none: the locale is the URL. A year-long cookie with no reader was dead weight.
Geist typefaceIBM Plex Sans Arabic keptOne family for Latin, Turkish and Arabic with drawn diacritics, so the three languages are one voice.

Found on the way

Defects fixed

All on screens this change restyles, which is why they are in it.

  • The rail's logo rendered emerald on its emerald tile, so the brand tile was empty.
  • Rooms cards printed a room's capacity as “N occupied”, so an empty room read “2 occupied” beside its Free badge.
  • The bed map's section headings reused form labels, so the page read “Building (optional)” and “Floor (optional) 4”.
  • The Rooms list view headed the occupancy column “Balance” and the actions column “Columns”.
  • Rooms rendered a second h1 under the page bar's.
  • A reserved count was lower-cased without a locale, which mangles Turkish İ.
  • The account card printed the email twice when no display name exists.
  • The mobile page bar let the breadcrumb run under the property switcher.
  • The sign-in page had no h1 on a phone once the slogan column is hidden.
  • Hard-coded hex colours on both sign-in screens bypassed the theme; they are tokens now.

Verification

What was run, and what it showed

  • pnpm check: format, lint, dependency boundaries, typecheck across 18 packages, 99 unit tests (including one that pins the page to a single h1, seen failing when the h1 is removed), docs check and the production build all pass.
  • pnpm test:browser: every one of the nine tests passed, but not all in a single run. After the sign-in redesign, seven of nine passed in one run, each signing in through the new page; the two failures were a 57-second database transaction and a sign-in where the email was typed before the form hydrated and then cleared — a race in the shared signIn test helper, not in the page. The arrivals spec was run three times with the machine's load average between 78 and 91 on 12 cores, and a different test timed out each time: once a check-in still pending after 15 seconds, once a refusal, once the post-sign-in redirect. Every test passed in at least one run. A regression would fail the same test every time; this is contention. It deserves a clean re-run on a quiet machine before merge.
  • Every screen above was captured signed in, in English and Arabic, at 1440px and at 390px. The sign-in and workspace screens show no console errors once the database is reachable.

During the work, another session committed the in-progress tree as PR #53 and switched this checkout back to main. The work was continued in its own worktree on that branch. Nothing was lost, but the PR's first commit predates the fixes this record describes.

For the team

Open decisions

A rendered image for the sign-in panelEduBoard's panel is a rendered photograph of silk; Ranza's is drawn in SVG from its own tokens. A rendered emerald-and-gold image would drop into the same slot if the team wants one.
PR #53's descriptionIt says the switcher “sets preferred_locale”. It does not; that was removed as dead before the commit. The description should be corrected when these commits are pushed.
Flags as language markersEmoji flags render as letter pairs on Windows, and a Saudi flag for Arabic names a country, not a language. Kept because it is the Leaders control; worth a deliberate decision before launch.
Merging at allThis is a rebrand: visual-reference.md now states the Leaders palette as the authority. That is a team decision, as the PR says.
